articles.t: GTA 6 leaker's latest video allegedly shows scenes from the final mission, as they indicate the leaks may have come to an end
articles.chapeau: Cyberleak is back with another GTA 6 leak they say shows snippets from the game's ending.
articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the leaker who's been releasing footage from Grand Theft Auto 6 for weeks now, is seemingly done posting leaks. Cyberleek released a new - seemingly final - video today which supposedly shows parts of the game's ending.
The leaker has indicated they may be done sharing footage as their goal of pumping their crypto coin had failed. Cyberleek recently said they'd release a 200GB build of the game if the coin hits $30m market cap, which it's nowhere near doing .
The coin has crashed in recent weeks after a major bump that coincided with the release of leaked footage showing co-protagonist Lucia fully naked , shortly after they released footage of co-protagonist Jason also nude .
Eurogamer has seen the latest footage, and it's not as dramatic as Cyberleek initially made it out to be. The footage does not appear to be of the game's ending sequence or final cutscene, though the location of where the action takes place could be a spoiler. The four-minute video ends with a montage of various locations and flyover footage of a city, set to Journey's Don't Stop Believin'.
There may be something there, but when viewed without proper context, it's hard to say what's actually being spoiled. Still, the footage is best avoided if you want to jump into the game fresh.
"The 30m was not reached, so no build," Cyberleek reportedly said in a message posted on their website. "Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk - worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project."
At the time of writing, Cyberleek's memecoin's market cap has dropped to $1.2m just three days after reaching its peak of $7.8m. It also seems they've abandoned the initial plan to tie certain gameplay leaks to the coin's market cap.
"The leeks stop here. For now," Cyberleek allegedly wrote, though it's worth keeping in mind that the leaker reappeared last week after going to ground following their initial leaks in August, seemingly in response to Rockstar parent company Take-Two initiating a massive investigation and issuing subpoenas to Discord and Microsoft.
Given recent history, Cyberleek could simply re-emerge yet again with a new scam and more footage. GTA 6's 19th November official launch is not far off, however, so their window is closing.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leaker Threatens Story Spoilers If Caught
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek says the latest leak is final one 'for now'
articles.txt:
Notorious Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek has threatened to reveal story spoilers if the hacking group is caught. In a new post accompanying Cyberleek's latest leaks, the person (or persons) said it has details on the game's ending and considered leaking it to "punish Take-Two greatly."
However, Cyberleek said leaking the ending would ruin the experience for players, and has only published out-of-context clips from the game's final missions so far. Still, don't think that Cyberleek isn't adverse to totally spoiling the game; they said, "the dead man's switch is active" and that story spoilers will be made public if Cyberleek is caught.
The latest unofficial videos of Grand Theft Auto 6 show new hairstyles and Lucia picking up a joint, which goes in her "Cigarettes & Drugs" inventory tab. More clothing customization is shown off, including what might be the first glimpse at the tie-in uniforms the Miami Heat will wear . Clips from what presumably is the final mission, "The End of the Road," are also included. People on Reddit have detailed what's shown if you want to read about the potential spoilers .
Image: Rockstar Games The rest of Cyberleek's message was about how it will not release the full build of the game after its $30 million crypto goal was not met. Cyberleek previously asked for "a donation" from players, and if those donations reached certain milestones, Cyberleek would release more clips from GTA 6 and eventually the game in its entirety. The clips released were of co-protagonist Lucia naked , because the internet is nothing if not horny. After thirsty folks got their fill, the Cyberleek coin's market cap sharply fell .
"Sad, the negativity — and how few believe anything real is behind this. CL was transparent about the token from day one: a donation, never an investment," Cyberleek said. "It changed nothing — influencers decided the story before the facts arrived. The Edict stands. The leeks stop here. For now."
If Cyberleek sticks to its guns, we won't see any more leaks from it ahead of GTA 6 's launch next month on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. But if Cyberleek is caught by the authorities, like other hacking groups , before the game's launch, it'll be interesting to see if Cyberleek's "dead man's switch" is real or an empty threat.

articles.t: GTA 6 leaker announces end of leaks, cancels full game release - VideoCardz.com
articles.chapeau: The anonymous GTA 6 leaker has abandoned its $30 million cryptocurrency demand. Cyberleek claims it has access to the game's ending and could still release story spoilers.
articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the anonymous group responsible for recent GTA 6 gameplay leaks, says it is ending its campaign against Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive. The announcement follows its unsuccessful attempt to push an associated cryptocurrency to a $30 million market capitalization in exchange for releasing what it claims is a complete playable build of the game.
In a three-part statement published on October 14, titled “The End of the Road,” Cyberleek confirmed that the target had not been reached. The group previously promised to release the entire single-player campaign if the cryptocurrency reached that valuation. It also offered to cancel the release if Take-Two committed to distributing the game on physical discs and issued a public apology.
Cyberleek now claims that distributing the build would involve anonymously uploading more than 200GB of data. The group argues that doing so carries considerable risk and it’s not worth it if the cryptocoin market cap has not been reached (how convenient).
The group also claims to have access to the game’s ending but says it has decided against publishing it. According to the statement, some of the recently released footage came from the final missions, although the clips were selected to avoid revealing major story details. Cyberleek claims a “dead man’s switch” remains active and could release story spoilers if the group is targeted. No evidence has been provided that such a mechanism exists.

articles.t: L'après GTA 6 : Rockstar Games promet de sortir des jeux plus vite, mais pas d'éviter les licenciements massifs — Frandroid
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 est annoncé avec tous les superlatifs possibles. Son studio de développement Rockstar Games s'offre un très beau portrait dans les colonnes de
articles.txt:
Cette fois c’est la bonne, GTA 6 semble bel et bien sur le point de sortir dans le commerce le 19 novembre 2026 au bout de huit très longues années de développement.
Dire que le jeu est attendu serait un euphémisme. On parle du successeur du jeu console et PC le plus vendus de tous les temps, GTA V et ses 230 millions d’exemplaires vendu (Minecraft le dépasse si l’on compte les sorties mobiles). Chaque bande annonce a cassé une partie d’Internet, jusqu’à une présentation détaillée sur Netflix qui était numéro un sur la plateforme de SVOD.
À l’approche de la sortie du jeu, Bloomberg signe un grand portrait de Rockstar Games , le studio de développement, de la plume de Jason Schreier. Il ne fallait rien de moins que le journaliste le plus réputé de l’industrie pour parler du jeu de tous les superlatifs dont on parle désormais comme l’une des plus grandes sorties de l’histoire du divertissement .
Dans cette grande enquête, on apprend que Rockstar Games compte désormais plus de 4711 employés. Ce nombre donne le vertige : ils étaient « seulement » 2441 lors du lancement de Red Dead Redemption 2 en 2018.
À titre de comparaison, Capcom compte 4000 employés pour l’ensemble du studio de développement qui travail à la fois sur Street Fighter , Monster Hunter et Resident Evil , entre autres.
Des studios occidentaux de jeux AAA classiques comme Larian Studios, Insomniac Games ou Naughty Dog tournent autour des 500 à 600 employés. Un très gros studio comme CD Projekt Red approche les 1000 employés, qui travaillent à la fois sur Cyberpunk et The Witcher.
Compte tenu du contexte de l’industrie, où Microsoft a encore récemment annoncé des milliers de licenciements , difficile de ne pas être inquiet pour l’avenir des employés de Rockstar Games .
Après la sortie de GTA 6 prévue le 19 novembre, le studio va être pleinement concentré au développement de la nouvelle version du GTA Online. En effet, seule la campagne solo est prévue pour cette année, mais c’est bien le mode en ligne qui interesse les très nombreux fans de la licence et peut faire exploser les revenus de l’éditeur Take Two.
Malgré tout, même en tenant compte du développement du mode en ligne, on a du mal à croire que Rockstar Games aura besoin de 4700 personnes. Sauf, bien sûr, si le studio veut produire rapidement une suite.
En conclusion de l’article de Jason Schreier, Rockstar Games évoque déjà l’après GTA VI. Le studio de développement aurait en effet mené de front une évolution de ses outils de développement et de son moteur de jeu, avec le développement du jeu lui-même.
Rockstar aimerait réutiliser ce travail pour son prochain projet et éviter de faire attendre les joueurs, et les investisseurs de Take-Two, pendant 8 ans.
Le moteur, les outils et l’équipe que nous avons mis en place au cours de ce projet nous permettront d’avancer plus rapidement », explique Phil Hooker, l’un des réalisateur du jeu. « Je suis convaincu que nous pourrons nous appuyer sur cette base et nous développer davantage en largeur qu’en profondeur pour créer des contenus encore plus captivants. »
Rockstar Games ne serait pas le premier studio à faire ce genre de promesses. La concrétisation est souvent plus complexe.
Quoi qu’il en soit, Rockstar Games nous promet que leur prochain jeu, que ce soit un nouveau Red Dead Redemption, GTA 7 ou un nouveau jeu, arrivera avant 2034.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leak Economy: $40 Builds, 7-Step Roadmap [2026]
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek's GTA 6 leak saga adds a $40 paywall and a 7-stage roadmap. What's confirmed, what's rumor, and what happens before Nov. 19 launch.
articles.txt:
The GTA 6 leak saga took a stranger turn this week. An anonymous account calling itself Cyberleek went quiet for more than a month after an August trailer leak, then came back on October 8, 2026 with a new video, a paywalled “development build,” and a seven-item roadmap that ends with a threat to release the entire game. As of October 14, 2026, neither Rockstar Games nor Take-Two Interactive has issued a public response to the latest claims, according to multiple outlets tracking the story. Grand Theft Auto VI is still scheduled to launch November 19, 2026, on Xbox Series X|S and other platforms , per Rockstar’s own store listing for the game .
What makes this round different from earlier GTA 6 leaks is the business model behind it. Cyberleek isn’t just dumping footage anymore. It’s selling access, tying a future “full build” release to a cryptocurrency market-cap target, and publishing a staged list of content drops like a marketing calendar. shattered.io has covered several of these individual moments as they broke. This piece steps back to look at the whole pattern: what’s confirmed, what’s pure claim, how it stacks up against gaming’s history of leaks and extortion, and what it actually means for Rockstar’s November launch.
Cyberleek first drew attention earlier this year, then went silent for over a month following an unrelated Netflix trailer moment for Grand Theft Auto VI. That silence broke on October 8, when the account resurfaced with a long unauthorized video. Shattered.io previously reported on the leak site’s return after two months of silence , and the pattern has held: go dark, resurface with something bigger, then escalate the demands.
This time the escalation included a new wrinkle. Rather than simply posting footage for free, Cyberleek began advertising a file for sale. Reports describe websites tied to the account offering a “GTA 6: Development Build” behind a paywall, a shift from leak-as-spectacle to leak-as-storefront. The account also followed up with additional clips days apart rather than one large dump, stretching the news cycle across most of October instead of burning it in a single afternoon.
According to posts attributed to the account, the file in question is labeled “GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1.08022025” and carries a price of $40 per download. Cyberleek’s own alleged statement put it bluntly: “DEVELOPMENT BUILD IS OUT: GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1.08022025 is up,” the account reportedly posted, according to Mashable’s coverage of the release update . A separate line attributed to the account framed the pricing around a missed crypto target: “The deal was 30 million marketcap and the build goes out. Cap was not hit. Build is out anyway. $40 per download. Pay it, then take the mirror.”
None of that confirms the file is real, complete, or actually what it claims to be. Shattered.io covered the earlier claim that the alleged build ran to roughly 200GB and was described as “playable” by the leaker, a figure that remains entirely unverified by any independent party. No security researcher, journalist, or Rockstar representative has confirmed downloading, running, or inspecting the file. Selling access to an unverified archive is also, on its face, a way to monetize curiosity regardless of whether the product behind the paywall does anything at all.
Alongside the paywalled file, the account reportedly published a roadmap listing seven planned content drops, each framed as a milestone toward the eventual release of the complete game. According to a report cited by The Times of India, the list read: “Mini Tank, Tank, Police Shootout, Beach Massacre, Fight Jet, Train vs. Train, The full build.” That’s the entire sequence, start to finish, as described in the alleged post.
Treat every row of that table as a claim, not a fact. shattered.io previously wrote about the moment this list first surfaced as a threatened “full drop” tied to specific features, and nothing in the reporting since has independently confirmed that any of the earlier-stage items are genuine footage from a current build of Grand Theft Auto VI, as opposed to recycled, fabricated, or unrelated material repackaged under the Cyberleek name.
The most unusual piece of this story is the crypto angle. Cyberleek reportedly tied the release of a complete, playable build to a $30 million market-capitalization target for a Solana-based meme coin carrying its name. shattered.io covered that threat directly when it first emerged, repo

articles.t: « Il y avait une certaine appréhension » GTA 6 : déjà adorée par les joueurs, la plus grande innovation du jeu aura donné des sueurs froides à Rockstar
articles.chapeau: Vertigineux, GTA 6 le sera autant pour les joueurs qu’il ne l’a été pour Rockstar Games, qui aura eu bien des difficultés à mettre en place sa plus grande innovation.
articles.txt:
Vertigineux, GTA 6 le sera autant pour les joueurs qu’il ne l’a été pour Rockstar Games, qui aura eu bien des difficultés à mettre en place sa plus grande innovation.
Vous pensiez qu’on en avait terminé avec les previews concernant GTA 6 ? Détrompez-vous. À 36 jours désormais de la sortie du jeu le plus attendu de l’année, mais aussi plus largement de la décennie, Rockstar Games ne compte pas ralentir la cadence. Pas plus que les médias qui ont eu la chance d’aller à la rencontre du studio. Et aujourd’hui, c’est désormais au tour de Bloomberg de nous en révéler davantage sur les coulisses de production de GTA 6, un jeu au développement difficile qui compte bien repousser toutes les limites de ce qu'on a connu.
Ce n’est en effet pas pour rien si le prochain titre de Rockstar aura mis autant de temps à voir le jour. Car si l’on enlève le temps de développement accordé à Red Dead Redemption 2 , ou encore des événements imprévus comme le COVID-19, de nombreux facteurs n’auront pas manqué de ralentir la production de GTA 6. Et comme le révèle Rob Nelson, co-directeur de Rockstar North, l’ambition du studio en fait partie. Notamment parce que l’équipe tenait absolument à repousser les limites de ce qu’il est possible de faire dans un monde ouvert avec deux protagonistes.
Forcément, cela a donc nécessité de la part de Rockstar la mise en place de nouveaux systèmes extrêmement complexes, dont la conception prendrait plusieurs années à être achevée. C’est d’ailleurs pour cela qu’il y avait « une certaine appréhension à se lancer dans ce projet » , confie le réalisateur de GTA 6. « Et puis il y a certaines personnes qui ont défendu cette idée : ‘On en a besoin. C’est un jeu qui parle d’un couple. Il faut que ce soit un couple’. Donc on a dû s’y tenir » , explique Nelson de façon quelque peu résolue.
Mais aujourd’hui, force est de constater que tous ces efforts en valaient la peine. Car alors même que GTA 6 n’est pas encore arrivé entre les mains du public, tout porte déjà à croire que Lucia et Jason sont amenés à devenir l’un des couples les plus emblématiques de l’histoire du jeu vidéo. Et certaines des nouveautés de gameplay du jeu seront là pour renforcer cette idée auprès des joueurs, tel que le fait de voir les deux héros s’échanger des SMS en cours de partie, ou entretenir leur relation via toutes sortes d’activités secondaires auxquelles il sera possible de prendre part.
Une promenade main dans la main dans un parc, une séance de sport commune à la salle, un cambriolage dans un magasin, une course poursuite avec les forces de l’ordre… Oui, tout cela fera partie de l’ADN même de GTA 6, en offrant non seulement aux joueurs des mécaniques de gameplay susceptibles de nourrir l’expérience de jeu, mais aussi d’approfondir la narration de son univers et de ses personnages. Reste maintenant à voir ce qu’il en sera réellement manette en main, dès le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series, et peut-être début 2027 sur PC.

articles.t: GTA 6 a pris 8 ans, mais Rockstar Games veut aller plus vite pour son prochain jeu
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 a pris 8 ans, mais Rockstar Games veut aller plus vite pour son prochain jeu - Après plus de 8 ans de travail sur GTA 6, Rockstar Games pense déjà à la suite. Le studio assure que ses futurs projets pourront avancer plus vite grâce
articles.txt:
Après plus de 8 ans de travail sur GTA 6, Rockstar Games pense déjà à la suite. Le studio assure que ses futurs projets pourront avancer plus vite grâce aux fondations techniques posées avec son prochain mastodonte. Une nouvelle particulièrement encourageante, alors que l’attente a été très longue depuis Red Dead Redemption 2.
GTA 6 marquera le premier grand jeu solo inédit de Rockstar Games depuis Red Dead Redemption 2, sorti en octobre 2018 sur Xbox One et PS4. Le titre arrivera le 19 novembre sur Xbox Series X|S et PS5, après une production de plus de 8 ans et 2 reports.
Dans une longue interview accordée à Bloomberg , les dirigeants Phil Hooker et Aaron Garbut ont expliqué que tout le travail réalisé pour GTA 6 ne sera pas abandonné une fois le jeu sorti. Le moteur, les outils de production et l’équipe réunie pour ce projet doivent au contraire permettre à Rockstar de raccourcir le développement de son prochain jeu.
Le moteur, les outils et l’équipe que nous avons construits au cours de ce projet nous permettront d’aller plus vite.
Phil Hooker estime que Rockstar pourra s’appuyer sur ces bases pour proposer des contenus plus ambitieux, sans devoir repartir de zéro à chaque nouveau projet. Selon lui, le studio cherchera davantage à étendre ce qui existe déjà qu’à faire grossir sans cesse ses productions.
Je suis convaincu que nous pouvons nous appuyer sur cette base et élargir davantage le projet plutôt que de le faire croître verticalement, afin de créer des contenus plus convaincants.
La promesse est importante. Avec des jeux toujours plus coûteux et longs à développer, il était facile d’imaginer que le prochain titre solo de Rockstar n’arriverait pas avant le milieu des années 2030. Le studio affirme désormais qu’il ne faudra pas attendre à nouveau 8 ans.
Aaron Garbut rappelle que GTA 6 a demandé de profondes transformations en interne. Rockstar a revu une grande partie de ses fondations techniques et de ses méthodes de travail, mais ce chantier semble désormais achevé.
Nous avons profondément modifié beaucoup de choses sur ce projet. Mais c’est désormais fait, et nous n’allons pas tout démanteler.
Bloomberg compare cette situation au passage de GTA III à GTA : Vice City. Ce dernier était sorti moins d’un an après son prédécesseur, car Rockstar avait déjà construit l’essentiel de ses outils et de ses fondations. Il ne faut évidemment pas s’attendre à un nouveau jeu aussi rapidement après GTA 6, mais cette comparaison illustre bien l’intérêt de conserver tout ce qui a été mis en place.
Cette déclaration est d’autant plus intéressante que Rockstar pourrait être tenté de se concentrer uniquement sur un hypothétique GTA 6 Online durant de nombreuses années. Le studio n’a encore rien officialisé à ce sujet, mais un mode en ligne paraît difficile à écarter après le succès durable de GTA Online.
Un tel service pourrait devenir une plateforme pensée sur le long terme, à l’image de Fortnite ou Roblox. Rockstar assure toutefois qu’il ne compte pas s’enfermer dans cette seule stratégie. Le studio évoque déjà son prochain jeu, ce qui laisse espérer qu’un nouveau grand projet solo est bien prévu après GTA 6.
Reste désormais à savoir quelle forme prendra ce jeu. Rockstar reviendra-t-il avec un nouveau GTA, un Red Dead Redemption inédit ou une licence totalement surprenante ? Il faudra patienter avant d’avoir une réponse, mais le plus rassurant est déjà là : le prochain gros jeu du studio ne devrait pas imposer une attente aussi interminable.

articles.t: GTA 6 : les 200 Go annoncés par Cyberleek ne sont pas la taille du jeu - GinjFo
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek affirme détenir une build de GTA 6 dépassant 200 Go. Ce chiffre lié à une version de développement présumée, ne permet pas d’estimer l’espace nécessaire pour installer le jeu sur PS5 ou Xbox.
articles.txt:
Dans un message du 12 octobre, Cyberleek affirme que la build de GTA 6 qu’il possède dépasse les 200 Go. Une nouvelle fois il menace une diffusion conditionnée à la capitalisation de sa cryptomonnaie.
Il y a cependant un important détail dans ces déclarations. Il s’agit d’un version de développement. Elle peut donc contenir des outils internes, des fichiers temporaires ou des ressources qui ne seront pas intégrées au jeu commercial. Elle peut aussi être moins optimisée. Du coup comparer directement ces 200 Go à la future installation de GTA 6 est trompeur.
Pour le moment Rockstar n’a publié aucune configuration officielle indiquant la place nécessaire sur le SSD d’une PS5 ou d’une Xbox Series X|S. Les 200 Go ne constituent donc ni un prérequis confirmé ni une indication fiable de la taille finale. Les consoles pourraient aussi recevoir des fichiers différents selon la plateforme ou les mises à jour.
La prudence vaut également pour les fichiers présentés en ligne comme une build jouable. Leur origine et leur contenu ne sont pas vérifiés et peuvent s’accompagner de logiciels malveillants et de virus.
L’information la plus utile dans toute cette histoire est que la taille de téléchargement de GTA 6 reste inconnue. Il faudra attendre une annonce de Rockstar ou les fiches officielles des boutiques avant de libérer de l’espace sur sa console.
La sortie du jeu est annoncée sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S le 19 novembre.

articles.t: Cyberleek a publié une nouvelle fuite de gameplay de GTA 6 — il se pourrait qu'elle contienne la mission finale du jeu
New GTA 6 Cyberleek video has story clips and one NSFW detail
articles.chapeau: We're not joking about the NSFW part.
articles.txt:
We thought we were done with notorious Grand Theft Auto VI leaker known only as Cyberleek , but we were proven wrong on Thursday with a fresh GTA 6 leak.
The still-anonymous leaker (or group of leakers) posted their first update since late August, in the form of a nearly 25-minute-long video that's easy enough to find on social media. It's our most detailed look yet at the hotly anticipated game from Rockstar, at least outside of the official "Extended Look" that aired on Netflix in August.
If you manage to find the video, be warned: Major portions of it are strictly not safe for work. It includes a lot of footage of Jason, the male protagonist, walking around completely nude, and everything is modeled in full detail. It's unclear if this is something you can actually do in the final game, or if Cyberleek used some kind of developer tools to pull it off. There are a couple of bits of evidence pointing to the latter; NPCs do not react at all to Jason's nudity, and at one point, the person playing the leaked build spawns a tank out of thin air, suggesting capabilities beyond what normal players will be able to do.
There is also a very brief clip of Lucia, the game's other protagonist, who is seen mostly nude at the very end of the video. There was some speculation earlier in the week that nudity would be part of the game, and it seems like it's at least partially confirmed now.
Beyond the NSFW bits, nothing in the video is all that surprising. We see a couple of different vehicular races, both of which are pre-empted by cutscenes introducing the characters in charge of racing in the countryside and on city streets. These cutscenes aren't especially spoiler-heavy, but if you're really precious about not seeing them ahead of release, you should probably avoid Cyberleek's latest GTA 6 leaks.
We also get a brief look at vehicle customization, which includes the ability to upgrade the engine, transmission, and other aspects of cars. There's also some footage of the game being played in first-person, both while driving and walking around. This was a popular feature Rockstar added to GTA 5 years after release (and incorporated into Red Dead Redemption II ), but it hasn't been shown in GTA 6 yet.

articles.chapeau: Cyberleek, the leaker behind GTA 6 info, says they’re stopping for now since their crypto didn’t hit the $30M goal. They’ve shared new gameplay but claim no full game will drop yet.
articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the leaker behind GTA 6 info, says they’re stopping for now since their crypto didn’t hit the $30M goal. They’ve shared new gameplay but claim no full game will drop yet.
Cyberleek, the anonymous person or group behind a series of GTA 6 leaks, says the leaks are stopping “for now” and that a claimed full playable build of the game won’t be released after their cryptocurrency failed to reach a $30 million market cap.
The announcement comes alongside another roughly four-minute video, this time showing Lucia getting a haircut, robbing a shop and playing pool. It also includes a sequence that Cyberleek suggests contains footage from the game’s final missions, although exactly what we’re seeing is difficult to establish. I’ll get into the footage below, after a potential spoiler warning. Don’t worry too much, though, as it really doesn’t show anything I would deem as a story spoiler.
In a three-part statement posted to their website on October 14, titled The End of the Road, Cyberleek addresses the earlier promise to release a playable build if the token reached a $30 million valuation . It is currently sitting at about $1.03 million, so not even close.
“The 30M was not reached, so no build,” they write. “Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk – worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project. Terms honored as written.”
To be clear, that target was the token’s market capitalisation, rather than $30 million in donations directly received by Cyberleek. Their possession of a complete playable build also remains a claim, even with the footage they’ve been releasing.
Cyberleek also claims to have the game’s ending and to have considered publishing it, before deciding that doing so would spoil the experience for players who had done nothing wrong. That would explain their apparent reluctance to release major story spoilers despite repeatedly threatening Take-Two. Everything we’ve seen from them so far has been mostly harmless: little snippets of side missions, lots of freeroam gameplay.
However, they say a “dead man’s switch” remains active and would release story spoilers. “Left alone, it never fires. Whoever removes CL chooses it,” the statement reads. What “removes” means here is unclear. I assume if they get arrested and taken to court or something.
Much of the remaining message is devoted to defending the cryptocurrency. Cyberleek says they sold twice, only withdrawing trading fees as previously announced, and blames other sellers for the subsequent collapse because they panicked and pulled out. They reject accusations of a rugpull and say their transactions can be checked on the blockchain.
They also insist the token was always presented as a donation, with no financial returns promised. My recollection of their earlier messaging is that they were fairly clear on that point: the money was supposedly going toward a vague secret project connected to their wider campaign against industry practices. But since the super secret project has presumably not been funded, it doesn’t look like Cyberleek plans on giving the cash back, either.
THE END OF THE ROAD (1/3) CL sold twice. Both times: trading fees only, as always announced. The first sale caused a cascade: everyone else sold, and CL was blamed for the crowd’s dump. The chain is public: what CL holds, sold, and delivered. What was promised was kept. The token was always a donation, never an investment. No returns promised, none implied. Rugpull talk comes from people who never opened the chain. Mostly YouTubers. Do not trust them. They have no idea what they are talking about. 14 Oct 2026, 13:08 THE END OF THE ROAD (2/3) CL has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly – but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy – why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished. Proof: the latest leek – clips from the final missions, out of context, revealing nothing. | The dead man’s switch is active – story spoilers only. Left alone, it never fires. Whoever removes CL chooses it. 14 Oct 2026, 13:08 THE END OF THE ROAD (3/3) The 30M was not reached, so no build. Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk – worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project. Terms honored as written. | Sad, the negativity – and how few believe anything real is behind this. CL was transparent about the token from day one: a donation, never an inve

articles.t: GTA 6 Leaker Is "Stopping For Now" as Website Goes Offline
articles.chapeau: The GTA 6 leaker's reign of terror could be over...for now. Their website is now offline, but they suggest they're not entirely done.
articles.txt:
With Grand Theft Auto 6 right around the corner, every new leak has the potential to be a major one. Once the game is out, the notorious CYBERLEEKS will be pretty much done, but the GTA 6 leaker has hinted that this could be the case already.
Let’s cut to the chase: The GTA 6 leaker threatened to leak a playable build of Grand Theft Auto VI from ‘Beginning to End’ if his cryptocurrency coin reached a market cap of $30 million. This did not happen.
As a result, the GTA 6 leaks are stopping, and their official website, where leaks and polls have been posted, is currently unavailable.
Here’s a statement from the now-defunct CYBERLEEKS site (thanks to @GTASixInfo ):
“CL (CYBERLEEKS) has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly – but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy – why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished. Proof: the latest leek – clips from the final missions, out of context, revealing nothing. The dead man’s switch is active – story spoilers only. Left alone, it never fires. Whoever removes CL chooses it.
The 30M was not reached, so no build. Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk – worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project. Terms honored as written. Sad, the negativity – and how few believe anything real is behind this. CL was transparent about the token from day one: a donation, never an investment. It changed nothing – influencers decided the story before the facts arrived. The Edict stands. The leeks stop here. For now.”
New GTA 6 leaks disappeared from the public eye following the Netflix reveal, and it seemed like we had safe, spoiler-free passage until November 19.
Hopefully, for everyone’s sake, to avoid key story spoilers, this is it, and they don’t trigger the alleged Dead Man’s Switch. The ‘for now’ will understandably also put GTA fans on edge, so we’ll see how it all plays out.

articles.t: 'The Leeks Stop Here. For Now' — GTA 6 Leaker Releases New Gameplay Video Showing Snippets of the Final Missions, Declares 'The End of the Road' After Crypto Scheme Collapses
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek has released a new GTA 6 gameplay video showing snippets of the ending, and declared "the end of the road" after their crypto scheme collapsed.
articles.txt:
The GTA 6 leaker has allegedly released a new unauthorized gameplay video which reportedly shows parts of the ending of the story, sparking significant spoiler concern among fans online. IGN will not report on the details of the leaked video.
Meanwhile, Cyberleek — the person or group responsible for the high-profile GTA 6 leaks that began in the summer — has suggested they will now stop leaking the game. They also claim they will not risk releasing an alleged 200GB build of GTA 6 because their memecoin failed to hit the $30 million market cap target that had been set for its release.
However, Cyberleek claims to have a "dead man's switch" for story spoilers, which they have reportedly threatened to flip if they are threatened, presumably by either Rockstar Games or parent company Take-Two.
Yesterday, we reported on how GTA 6 fans were celebrating the crash of the Cyberleek memecoin after the leaker had tied various types of gameplay leaks to its market cap, ranging from $5 million to $25 million. The leaker also threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap.
Earlier this week, a number of gameplay clips were reportedly leaked after market cap goals were hit, including gameplay that allegedly shows Lucia fully naked, and, more recently, the alleged leak of a “Lucia closeup 4k” video.
Cyberleek then threatened to release a new unauthorized GTA 6 gameplay video every day, assuming the memecoin market cap targets were met, and launched yet another gameplay poll designed to encourage spending on the memecoin.
However, the Cyberleek memecoin crashed, with a current market cap of $1.2 million, down from a high of $7.8 million on October 11. With those targets now pretty much impossible, it sounds like Cyberleek's crypto scheme has come to an end.
In a new message reportedly posted to their website, Cyberleek declared "the end of the road." In the post, Cyberleek defended their actions from crypto scam allegations, and said Take-Two was "punished enough." "The ending stays unpublished," Cyberleek allegedly insisted in the message. They claimed that while the latest leak does show clips from the final missions of the game, out of context they do not spoil the story.
It's fair to say many fans have taken issue with that suggestion, and are already taking steps to avoid spoilers online.
Cyberleek's message also suggests that the build of GTA 6 they allegedly have access to will not be released because the $30 million market cap was not reached. Cyberleek had said they were raising funds for some mystery project, although many didn't believe the claim. "Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk," they said, "worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project." They said the memecoin should have been considered a "donation," not an "investment," and hit out at "influencers" who claimed otherwise.
Of course, Cyberleek may release further gameplay and continue with their crypto scheme anyway. They may even release the build they allegedly have. For now though, the more pressing concern is avoiding spoilers sparked by today's leaked video.
Fans had spent the last week calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and is likely to do so again ahead of GTA 6’s official release date, if they haven’t already. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000.
Earlier this week, IGN reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked . A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggests access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to nudity in any way, which suggests this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats and won’t be possible in the official release.
One theory is that Cyberleak was able to access this state for both Lucia and Jason because in at least one mission players will see both characters naked, perhaps in a nudist resort. As it stands, this is all speculation, and it is unknown if GTA 6 will feature either character naked at any point — officially at least.

articles.t: Rockstar's next game won't take eight years to make: "The engine, the tools and the team we've built during GTA 6 will allow us to do things more quickly"
articles.chapeau: Developer's team has more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2's launch in 2018, with over 4,000 working in development and QA
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games has more than doubled its workforce to develop Grand Theft Auto 6, and is adamant that it won't take another eight years to complete its next title.
In a wide-ranging interview with Bloomberg , Rockstar senior leadership said that when Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in 2018, the studio had 2,441 employees.
By 2026, Rockstar employed 4,711 staff across 12 offices. Of these, 4,020 work in development and QA, while 690 are in publishing.
Rockstar's leadership stated that future games will be developed more quickly, as GTA 6 "is a foundation upon which they can build new content at a faster pace."
"The engine, the tools and the team we've built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly," said co-head of development Phil Hooker. "I feel confident that we can build on top of this and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content."
GTA 6 was first announced in 2023 with a planned 2025 release . The launch was postponed to May 26, 2026 , and later rescheduled to its current date, November 19 .
Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recalled informing Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick about both delays. "I think he said, 'You're kidding. Please tell me you're kidding.' But once we talked through why, he got it."
"And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say, 'You'd just better figure out how to ship it.' And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we've all played those games. It's not great."
Zelnick previously told GamesIndustry.biz that he wasn't "in the least" bit worried about the impact that delays could have on the business.
"As you know, occasionally across our entire company, including 2K and our mobile business, at times more time is required to polish a title to ensure that it's released in its best possible form. And of course it'll release in the same fiscal year as the prior date."
"At the end of the day it's our responsibility to do the right thing for our consumers, and that means delivering the best possible entertainment experience."
Elsewhere in the interview, the topic of leaks was addressed. Rockstar was hit with its first set of leaks in September 2022 , which were caused by a "network intrusion" and resulted in 90 in-development video clips of the game being shared.
"It feels like somebody's wading through your dirty washing. It's like they're inside your head," said Rockstar North co-head Aaron Garbut. "You see your early work out there. Nobody's ever supposed to see that. It's really weirdly invasive. And so it's quite hard to deal with on an emotional level."
Security at Rockstar was heightened as a result, leading to the elimination of remote work in April 2024 . "The idea that we would have the game in that many environments is something that I think the security team would not love," said Kolbe.
"I think if we did not have a game that people wanted to steal as much, maybe it would be an easier conversation."
The developer is currently addressing another set of leaks from a hacker group that appears to possess a build of the game. The group began circulating footage in August .
Earlier this week, the group released additional footage and threatened to leak the full build, including the story mode, if Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, does not comply with its demands.

articles.t: GTA 6 was originally Project Americas and covered "big swaths" of country's north and south, Rockstar reveals, in interview tackling crunch, delays, and leaks
articles.chapeau: In a wide-ranging GTA 6 interview, Rockstar has discussed crunch, the game's origins, leaks, delays and more.
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games has revealed the original codename for Grand Theft Auto 6 was Project Americas, and that its intention was for the game to cover large areas of land in both the north of the country and the south.
The information comes from a wide-ranging interview with Rockstar on Bloomberg , which charted the beginnings of the GTA 6 project as well as the notable moments since: delays, game leaks, trailer releases, and more.
Bloomberg heard that Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson took a group of staff to Miami in 2015 for the game's first research trip, and that Project Americas - as the game was then known - "aimed to feature big swaths of land across both North and South America", before being scaled down to Miami and its surrounding areas. The original idea was to develop the game alongside Red Dead Redemption 2 , but as the western project grew in scope and ambition, Project Americas was pushed back several years.
But lots changed after the release of Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar would nearly double in size, for starters - moving from 2,441 employees to 4,711 across 12 offices, the article noted. Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser, who'd written many of the previous GTA games, also left the company, prompting promotions for Nelson, Aaron Garbut, and Phil Hooker, who stepped into head of development roles.
By 2019, Rockstar had the skeleton of GTA 6 and the dual-protagonist hook of Jason and Lucia living their crime fantasy together, but the more granular details and mechanical intricacies of the game took longer, especially when the Covid-19 pandemic hit, forcing people to work from home. "Trying to keep a team together through that is really challenging," Nelson said.
Red Dead Redemption 2 also painted Rockstar as a company working with extreme levels of crunch - something Tom Phillips revealed in an investigation for Eurogamer . Rockstar acknowledged this in the Bloomberg interview, with Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar's head of publishing, stating it was "a real moment for Rockstar to look at itself".
"We all looked at each other and said, 'We're not doing it again like this,'" she added. "It's not been perfect, but it's certainly better than Red Dead 2 was. Anytime I say we haven't crunched, someone is going to say, 'I did.' And I don't want to get into arguments with individual teams or individual people. But I think we did things differently, and I'm proud of that."
Bloomberg reportedly spoke to "dozens" of Rockstar employees who "mostly expressed positive sentiment" regarding what Kolbe said, acknowledging improvements in areas such as crunch and removing managers who were abusive or tough to work with. However, Rockstar is currently embroiled in an employment tribunal in Scotland after unceremoniously firing 34 employees - 31 of them from its Rockstar North office - for what it alleged was gross misconduct but the fired employees called union-busting. We've been covering the tribunal's hearings as they've happened. It's expected to conclude at the end of the week.
As GTA 6 began to take shape, Rockstar suffered one of its biggest setbacks ever, as a phishing attack gained access to the company's Slack in 2022 and leaked unfinished footage of the game . Aaron Garbut said in response: "It feels like somebody's wading through your dirty washing. It's like they're inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody's ever supposed to see that. It's really weirdly invasive. And so it's quite hard to deal with on an emotional level."
As development progressed, it became clear Rockstar needed more time to finish the game. GTA 6's first trailer , aired in 2023, promised the game would be released in 2025, but Rockstar would move this date to May 2026 to allow more time. Then Rockstar realised it wouldn't be able to finish the game in time for that date either. Kolbe recalled phoning Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar's owner Take-Two, to tell him the news.
"I think he said, 'You're kidding. Please tell me you're kidding,'" Kolbe recalled. "But once we talked through why, he got it. And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say, 'You'd just better figure out how to ship it.' And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we've all played those games. It's not great."
Rockstar did not comment on the ongoing leaks of GTA 6 footage by the group or persons known as Cyberleek du

articles.t: GTA 6 file size leaked by Cyberleek and it is absolutely massive
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 is going to take up a serious amount of hard drive space, as the game's most famous leaker reveals the size of an early build.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 is going to take up a serious amount of hard drive space, as the game’s most famous leaker reveals the size of an early build.
Aside from constant downloads, one of the biggest annoyances with modern gaming is the never-ending battle for hard drive space.
Some games are worse than others in hogging up room. Call Of Duty games, between the campaign, multiplayer, and Zombies, are always a chonker approaching 200GB when combined together. Open world games are typically a nuisance too, with GTA 5 and Cyberpunk 2077 hovering around 100GB, depending on your platform.
As such, Rockstar’s highly anticipated GTA 6 was always expected to be on the beefy side, and now that seems to have been confirmed.
The info comes from noted GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek, who has been posting clips from the game in an attempt to earn cryptocurrency from fans. After causing havoc a few months ago, the leaker reappeared recently with nude clips and threats to release the entire game online.
As part of the latter threat, Cyberleek claims the ‘playable build’ of GTA 6 takes up over 200GB.
Sign up to the GameCentral newsletter for the latest GTA 6 news, reviews of new games you should play and exclusive analysis of the biggest stories of the week.
However, there are some caveats to this figure. Firstly, it’s unclear what build Cyberleek actually has. All signs suggest it is an early debug version, and these are typically larger than the final release because the files haven’t been compressed yet.
It’s also not clear whether his build includes the main story campaign, as he’s showed virtually nothing of it. If it doesn’t then that is going to mean the final file size is even bigger.
The full playable GTA 6 build is over 200GB, according to CyberLeek, who plans to leak it if his cryptocurrency reaches a $30M market cap. pic.twitter.com/SMfgwNuEVj
Bearing these two factors in mind the file size could be reduced to something around 150GB, but it’s difficult to say without concrete knowledge of what Cyberleek actually has access to.
We’ll likely get concrete numbers around GTA 6’s file size in the run-up to launch next month, from insiders with access to backend store listings.
Whatever the size ends up being, it will only get larger when the inevitable online component comes out – although that might prove be a separate download from the base game.
GTA 6 is set to launch across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19, 2026. According to reports , the PC version is expected in early 2027.

articles.t: Rockstar Responds to GTA 6 Leaks, Explains Why They Hurt So Much
articles.chapeau: Rockstar Games responds to GTA 6 leaks, explaining their emotional impact on developers & why its next release should take less time to make.
articles.txt:
X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share using Native tools Share Copied to clipboard Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 leaks and why they were so upsetting for its developers. In a new Bloomberg interview, the studio explained how having unfinished work shared online affected the team behind Grand Theft Auto VI .
In an interview with Bloomberg Businessweek, Rockstar Games reflected on the massive September 2022 leak that exposed dozens of videos of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay . While the footage gave fans their first unofficial look at the next Grand Theft Auto , it was a deeply uncomfortable experience for the people making it.
According to Rockstar head of development Aaron Garbut, the leak felt like an invasion of the team’s personal creative process. “It feels like somebody’s wading through your dirty washing,” Garbut told Bloomberg. “It’s like they’re inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody’s ever supposed to see that. It’s really weirdly invasive. And so it’s quite hard to deal with on an emotional level.”
The footage also circulated before the game was ready to be shown publicly. For developers who had spent years working on Grand Theft Auto VI , that meant having their early work judged before they had the chance to finish it. Garbut’s comments offer a more personal explanation of why the incident hurt so much.
Of course, this isn’t the first time Rockstar has addressed leaks publicly. In August, the studio issued an apology to fans after a string of GTA 6 footage leaked before the Extended Look. “It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time.”
While Rockstar doesn’t make any new comments about the 2026 GTA 6 leaks specifically, the Bloomberg interview does give us some insight into how upsetting and challenging leaks of the much-anticipated game has been for the team behind Grand Theft Auto VI .
The interview also contains some promising news for fans wondering how long they’ll have to wait for whatever Rockstar makes next. According to Bloomberg, the studio’s leaders say their next release won’t take another eight years.
Rockstar head of development Phil Hooker explained that the technology and team built during GTA 6 ’s development should help the studio move faster in the future. “The engine, the tools and the team we’ve built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly,” Hooker said.
Garbut also revealed that Rockstar has already completed major foundational changes during this project. Going forward, the studio intends to build on that work rather than tear it apart and start again.
That doesn’t confirm GTA 7 , a new Red Dead Redemption , or a release date for either. However, it suggests that the lengthy development of Grand Theft Auto VI has created a foundation Rockstar believes it can use to deliver future projects more quickly.

articles.t: Original GTA 6 Leaks Were "Weirdly Invasive"
articles.chapeau: In a new sweeping interview with Rockstar Games, some more perspective has been shed on the original batch of leaks that struck GTA 6.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has been at the center of countless leaks, with the ongoing CYBERLEEK situation seeing gameplay footage shared online before Rockstar Games could reveal it themselves. Some of the material has even included explicit content that the developer likely never intended for the public to see.
However, this isn’t the first time Rockstar has faced such a situation. In September 2022, a phishing attack exposed dozens of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay clips, with a new Bloomberg interview revealing just how difficult the incident was for the development team to deal with.
Aaron Garbut, one of GTA 6’s development leads, reflected on the 2022 leaks in an interview with Bloomberg , describing the experience as deeply uncomfortable.
The leaked footage showed an early version of the game, prompting criticism of its graphics and animations despite the project still being years away from release. Although the individual responsible was eventually arrested, the footage had already spread across the internet, leaving Rockstar with little control over the public’s perception of its unfinished work.
Garbut compared the experience to “somebody’s wading through your dirty washing,” explaining how exposing unfinished work to millions of people felt like an invasion of privacy. He also described the incident as “weirdly invasive” and “quite hard to deal with on an emotional level.”
While his comments refer to the 2022 incident, Rockstar is now dealing with another major leak through CYBERLEEK , who has continued to share gameplay snippets online. Given the impact of the original incident, it’s understandable that the latest leaks could bring back similar feelings for those working on the game.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' Cyberleek release updates: What leaked, what's next
articles.chapeau: Maybe don't watch these videos on your work device.
articles.txt:
If you simply can't get enough of Grand Theft Auto VI prior to its Nov. 19 release, there are still new GTA 6 leaks coming out.
Cyberleek , the anonymous entity that has been leaking clips from a pre-release build of GTA 6 since August, made their grand return in October after about a month of silence. Last week, Cyberleek posted a 24-minute video that seemed to show some story sequences and a glimpse of the male protagonist Jason rendered completely nude. That wasn't the end of it.
And, as Cyberleek said they would, nude clips of the female protagonist Lucia soon followed. On top of that, Cyberleek is now threatening to release a development build of the game, and according to Dextero, may have already done so . Websites affiliated with Cyberleek include a link to a file named GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1, locked behind a $40 paywall.
It should go without saying that downloading files from a sketchy website is not a wise idea, nor is purchasing illegal content that violates Rockstar's copyright.
Cyberleek returned this week with more clips that you definitely should not watch at work.
That's because these new clips all center on the female protagonist, Lucia, nude. In the clips, Lucia does mundane things like walk around Vice City, drive a vehicle, and parachute off a skyscraper while wearing little to no clothes (OK, so not entirely mundane, actually). It doesn't seem like anything new has been posted since Monday morning, though.
One thing to note about these clips: The nudity doesn't appear to be a normal element of the gameplay, but rather some type of mod. Rockstar has designed its last couple of big open-world adventures around extremely reactive NPCs, and none of them react at all to seeing Jason or Lucia nude in these leaked clips. Between that, and another clip from last week where the player spawns a tank out of thin air, it sure seems like developer tools are being used to achieve outcomes that will not be possible in the final game.
In other words, don't expect to be able to streak around Vice City in the nude on Nov. 19.
On websites associated with Cyberleek, the leaker threatened to release a full playthrough of the entire GTA 6 story if their memecoin reached $30 million in market value. The leaker also threatened to release a development build of the game if Rockstar failed to meet their demands to release GTA 6 on a physical disc. There's just one problem: The coin is tanking.
IGN reported a market cap of just $1.7 million, well below any of the stretch goals specified by Cyberleek, and certainly not even close to the $7.8 million high it reached on Oct. 11. Despite this, Cyberleek may have made good on their threat to release a development build of the game.
Dextero is reporting that the development build has been posted online, locked behind a $40 paywall. In addition, a Cyberleek website with all of the leaked clips now includes this update, posted on Oct. 13: " DEVELOPMENT BUILD IS OUT: GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1.08022025 is up. The deal was 30 million marketcap and the build goes out. Cap was not hit. Build is out anyway. $40 per download. Pay it, then take the mirror."
Because the leaker is anonymous, and because it would be illegal and dangerous to download mystery files from an unverified website, we can't confirm that this development build is real, or that it was even directly posted by Cyberleek.
However, if there is now a development build floating around the web, expect to see far more GTA 6 leaks in the weeks leading up to the Nov. 19 release date.
Alternatively, you could wait and play the game when it actually comes out. You can preorder the game now .
A Cyberleek website includes a poll about what type of Lucia content to release next. The poll is set to end on Oct. 14, with the leading option as "Race track."
It seems extremely likely that more clips featuring Lucia are set to be released any day now.

articles.t: Cyberleek drops new NSFW Lucia videos, threatens to release GTA 6 in full
articles.chapeau: Only about a month until the game is out.
articles.txt:
Notorious Grand Theft Auto VI leaker Cyberleek is back with a vengeance, it seems.
The anonymous video poster went dark after the big Netflix trailer in late August, but returned last week with a big, chunky 24-minute clip that featured story cutscenes, auto races, and the male protagonist Jason fully nude. Over the weekend and into Monday morning, Cyberleek shared some more clips that we won't link to, but can be easily found on social media. The new clips largely revolve around the female protagonist Lucia, and also show her completely nude, doing things like walking around Vice City or parachuting off a tall building.
In addition, Cyberleek posted a warning on their website claiming that if their memecoin reached a market cap of $30 million, they would release a video showing a full playthrough of the game's story prior to release. The same post also included a demand for publisher Take-Two to apologize for not releasing the game on disc and to rectify that issue. It is extremely unlikely the company could fire up disc manufacturing for GTA 6 in a timely fashion, even if the publisher wanted to negotiate with the leaker. At this point, there is no sign of that happening.
Just like in the videos featuring a nude Jason, the nude Lucia videos seem a little fishy in the sense that NPCs don't react to their nudity at all. Given that recent Rockstar games are built entirely around believable NPC interactions, that would suggest the nudity is not a regularly accessible feature in the final game and is being achieved through the use of developer tools.

articles.t: L'auteur des leaks de GTA 6 affirme que le jeu pèse 200 Go, les joueurs n'ont plus qu'à faire de la place
articles.chapeau: Les dernières fuites autour de GTA 6 sont tombées et cette fois-ci, on parle de 200 Go de stockage pour installer le jeu sur sa console. C’est en tout cas
articles.txt:
Les dernières fuites autour de GTA 6 sont tombées et cette fois-ci, on parle de 200 Go de stockage pour installer le jeu sur sa console. C’est en tout cas ce que rapporte Cyberleek, le groupe de pirates qui est à l’origine des dernières fuites autour du hit de Rockstar.
Cyberleek affirme que la version de développement de GTA 6 dépasse les 200 Go, même si le poids final du jeu reste inconnu. Une telle taille représenterait près de la moitié du stockage d’une Xbox Series S 512 Go, mais la version commerciale pourrait être plus légère. Cyberleek promet encore des fuites avant la sortie du 19 novembre, tandis que Take-Two tente d’identifier les responsables avec l’aide de plusieurs plateformes. Cyberleek fait beaucoup parler de lui depuis plusieurs semaines. Le groupe s’est d’abord fait remarquer avec des images d’une build de développement avant la présentation officielle de GTA 6 sur Netflix . Puis rebelote récemment avec un fichier ZIP qui contient 25 minutes de gameplay . Bref, Cyberleek est la bête noire de Rockstar.
Et récemment, Cyberleek nous apprend que la version de développement qu’il utilise pour partager des images dépasse les 200 Go de stockage . On parle donc de la moitié du stockage d’une Xbox Series S de 512 Go et près d’un tiers pour une PS5 avec 825 Go.
GTA 6 will reportedly be over 200GB in size. Cyberleek claims the full playable development build is 200+GB. pic.twitter.com/egPV9es2pn
Mais rappelons toutefois que Rockstar n’a pas communiqué le poids officiel sur PC. Et puis de toute façon, le studio n’a même pas évoqué ce portage . Mais récemment, des rumeurs se sont rejointes sur le fait que la sortie de GTA 6 sur PC aurait lieu en début d’année 2027 .
Et puis précisons qu’une version de développement n’est pas identique au jeu final . On trouve dedans des outils pour les équipes de Rockstar, des fichiers tests et parfois des éléments qui sont supprimés lors de la sortie de la version commerciale.
Mais quoi qu’il en soit, on s’attend à une taille conséquente pour GTA 6 , sans doute entre 100 et 150 Go face à l’immensité du monde ouvert. Et puis on se base aussi sur Red Dead Redemption 2 et les images de GTA 6 qui montrent un monde ouvert ultra-détaillé avec de nombreuses mécaniques de gameplay.
Forcément, il ne faudra pas être surpris à la sortie si le jeu de Rockstar demande beaucoup de stockage sur la PS5 et la Xbox Series . Rappelons que c’est le 19 novembre prochain que sortira le jeu sur console. Pour beaucoup de joueurs, il s’agit de l’un des plus grands événements de ces dernières années.
Mais tout n’est pas rose et la colère gronde toutefois puisque Take-Two assume qu’il n’y aura pas de version disque de GTA 6 . Les joueurs pourraient toutefois avoir un lot de consolation puisque des rumeurs nous parlent d’un poster de la carte de Leonida où se déroule l’intrigue du jeu inclus dans la boîte physique pour toute précommande .
C’est donc dans un mois que sort GTA 6 et d’ici là, Cyberleek risque encore de faire parler de lui . Le groupe de pirates promet de publier la build complète de la version PC si leur objectif de 30 millions de dollars en cryptomonnaie est atteint .
Bref, Cyberleek a beau expliquer que son geste est motivé par le fait de dénoncer l’absence de disque physique pour GTA 6 , impossible de ne pas y voir une motivation opportuniste qui profite de l’engouement autour du jeu.
Take-Two ne se laisse pas faire. La maison mère de Rockstar a demandé en août dernier des informations détenues par Microsoft et Discord auprès de la justice pour identifier les comptes qui ont participé aux fuites. Take-Two s’est également tourné vers Google et X pour obtenir des informations précieuses.
Est-ce que Cyberleek sera mis hors d’état de nuire avant la sortie de GTA 6 ? Réponse dans le prochain épisode.

articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC : la fenêtre de sortie a fuité, et l’attente s’annonce bien plus courte que prévu
articles.chapeau: Les joueurs PC n’auront pas à ronger leur frein bien longtemps. Rockstar viserait le premier trimestre 2027 pour lancer GTA 6 sur ordinateur, à peine quelques mois après les consoles.
articles.txt:
Les joueurs PC n’auront pas à ronger leur frein bien longtemps. Rockstar viserait le premier trimestre 2027 pour lancer GTA 6 sur ordinateur, à peine quelques mois après les consoles.
Personne n’osait l’espérer. Selon GamesBeat , qui cite quatre sources anonymes au fait des plans du studio, la version PC de Grand Theft Auto VI arriverait entre janvier et mars 2027. Les possesseurs de PS5 et de Xbox Series X|S, eux, découvriront Vice City le 19 novembre, date confirmée sur le site officiel de Rockstar après deux reports . Contacté, le studio n’a pas commenté.
Chez Rockstar, l’attente se compte d’ordinaire en saisons. GTA V avait mis dix-neuf mois à rejoindre le PC, Red Dead Redemption 2 un peu plus d’un an. Au printemps, d’anciens développeurs du studio n’envisageaient pas de portage avant 2027 . En mai, Strauss Zelnick, PDG de Take-Two, défendait encore cette doctrine devant Bloomberg : « Rockstar commence toujours par la console ». Dans le même entretien, il reconnaissait que le PC peut peser « 45 à 50 % des ventes » d’un blockbuster. L’argument porte, pour un jeu dont le budget dépasserait, selon les rumeurs, deux milliards de dollars.
GamesBeat avance un autre levier : FiveM, la plateforme de serveurs roleplay rachetée par Rockstar en 2023, qui tourne exclusivement sur PC.
Le calendrier tombe aussi en pleine tempête pour Sony. Publié le 29 septembre, le jailbreak Relapse ouvre en quelques secondes les PS5 restées sous un firmware 13.60 ou antérieur . Dans le même temps, des émulateurs PC comme KytyPS5 font déjà tourner des jeux PS5. GTA 6 devrait échapper à l’exploit, que le firmware 14.00 neutralise. Une version PC officielle disponible dès l’hiver priverait toutefois les bidouilleurs de leur meilleure motivation.

articles.txt:
GTA 6 pourrait finalement arriver sur PC bien plus vite que ne le laissait penser l’historique de Rockstar Games. Une nouvelle indiscrétion évoque une fenêtre de sortie étonnamment proche de celle des consoles. Une information à prendre avec prudence, puisque le studio n’a encore rien officialisé.
GTA 6 sortira le 19 novembre 2026 sur Xbox Series X|S et PS5, mais Rockstar Games n’a toujours pas annoncé de version PC. Selon un nouveau rapport de GamesBeat , celle-ci serait néanmoins prévue au cours du premier trimestre 2027.
Le média affirme avoir obtenu cette information auprès de 4 sources issues de l’industrie, toutes anonymes afin de préserver leurs relations professionnelles. Rockstar Games n’aurait pas répondu à sa demande de commentaire avant la publication de l’article.
Si cette fenêtre se confirme, les joueurs PC n’auraient donc à patienter que quelques mois après la sortie sur consoles. Ce serait un changement notable pour Rockstar, dont les précédentes productions ont souvent connu un délai bien plus long avant leur arrivée sur ordinateur.
La comparaison avec GTA 5 est particulièrement frappante. Sorti en septembre 2013 sur Xbox 360 et PS3, le jeu n’avait débarqué sur PC qu’en avril 2015, soit près de 19 mois plus tard.
Red Dead Redemption 2 avait de son côté connu un délai plus mesuré. Disponible sur consoles en octobre 2018, il était arrivé sur PC en novembre 2019, un peu plus d’un an après.
GamesBeat avance que Rockstar aurait tout intérêt à élargir rapidement l’audience de GTA 6. Le budget de production du jeu dépasserait les 2 milliards de dollars, selon les informations évoquées par le média, tandis que la version PC représenterait une nouvelle opportunité commerciale majeure.
Cette sortie pourrait aussi avoir un rôle important pour l’avenir du jeu en ligne. Rockstar a acquis Cfx.re en août 2023, l’équipe derrière FiveM, une plateforme très populaire de serveurs roleplay sur GTA 5. Or, cette activité repose entièrement sur la version PC.
Rockstar souhaiterait intégrer des outils de création de contenus générés par les utilisateurs dans GTA 6. Une disponibilité rapide sur PC faciliterait logiquement le développement de serveurs communautaires et de contenus similaires.
Le multijoueur de GTA 6 reste pour le moment totalement absent de la communication officielle de Rockstar. Le jeu est même présenté comme une expérience solo dans une FAQ publiée par PlayStation en juin. Pourtant, Dan Clancy, PDG de Twitch, s’attend déjà à son lancement en 2027 après avoir échangé avec Rockstar au sujet des créateurs de contenu et des projets du studio.
Bloomberg présentait néanmoins cette déclaration comme l’anticipation du dirigeant, et non comme une information communiquée par Rockstar. Kotaku avait contacté le studio à ce sujet, sans obtenir de réponse. GTA Online avait été lancé quelques semaines après GTA 5, tandis que Red Dead Online était arrivé après l’aventure principale de Red Dead Redemption 2. Une sortie séparée ne constituerait donc pas une surprise.
Cette information fait écho aux propos d’Andy Robinson en septembre. Le journaliste de VGC indiquait alors avoir entendu des « bruits » autour d’une sortie PC plus rapide que prévu .
Il ne donnait alors aucune date et ne présentait pas ces éléments comme une annonce de Rockstar. Le rapport de GamesBeat apporte désormais une fenêtre plus précise, mais il doit lui aussi être considéré comme une rumeur tant que le studio ne communique pas officiellement.
Rockstar Games a déjà repoussé GTA 6 à deux reprises afin de peaufiner le jeu. Take-Two a récemment réaffirmé la sortie du 19 novembre 2026 sur consoles et indiqué que le titre se trouvait dans sa phase finale de finition et de débogage. Si la version PC vise réellement le premier trimestre 2027, elle devra donc répondre aux mêmes exigences de qualité avant d’être commercialisée.
La sortie de GTA 6 est prévue pour le 19 novembre 2026 sur Xbox Series X|S et PS5.

articles.t: GTA 6 : Cyberleek dévoile la taille du fichier sur PS5 et Xbox, il est vraiment colossal
articles.chapeau: CyberLeek affirme qu’une build de GTA 6 dépasse les 200 Go sur PS5 et Xbox Series, faisant grimper la pression avant novembre 2026. Jusqu’où ce fichier pourrait-il bousculer votre stockage ?
articles.txt:
CyberLeek affirme qu’une build de GTA 6 dépasse les 200 Go sur PS5 et Xbox Series, faisant grimper la pression avant novembre 2026. Jusqu’où ce fichier pourrait-il bousculer votre stockage ?
Le prochain monstre de Rockstar Games ne sera pas seulement gigantesque sur la carte. Selon le leaker CyberLeek , une build jouable de GTA 6 dépasserait les 200 Go , de quoi affoler les possesseurs de PS5 et de Xbox Series X|S déjà à court de SSD.
Au 13 octobre 2026, la taille de fichier officielle de GTA 6 n’apparaît toujours pas sur le PlayStation Store ni sur le Xbox Store, mais la sortie console est bien fixée au 19 novembre 2026, avec préchargement dès le 12 novembre. Alors, combien de Go faudra-t-il vraiment libérer sur votre console ?
CyberLeek affirme qu’un build complet et jouable de GTA 6 dépasse les 200 Go. D’après Notebookcheck, ce chiffre vient d’une version de développement interne, utilisée pour les tests et les vidéos leakées, et reprise par des comptes spécialisés comme GTA 6 Info sur X.
Il faut surtout comprendre qu’une build de développement ne correspond pas à la taille d’installation finale. Elle embarque des outils, des données de test et des assets en doublon. Notebookcheck rappelle qu’une archive de développement de GTA 5 avait déjà atteint 192 Go alors que le jeu pèse environ 95 Go sur PS5 et 105 Go sur PC.
Le monde ouvert de GTA 6 , situé à Leonida autour de Vice City, est annoncé comme environ deux fois plus vaste que celui de GTA 5 , avec beaucoup plus de détails. Logiquement, la taille de téléchargement sera nettement supérieure aux 95 Go actuels du précédent opus sur PS5.
Certains Call of Duty: Black Ops dépassent déjà les 200 Go, prouvant qu’un AAA console peut atteindre ce palier. La plupart des estimations sérieuses situent toutefois la taille d’installation de GTA 6 dans une fourchette de 150 à 200 Go. Les 200+ Go évoqués par CyberLeek semblent représenter la borne haute, pas forcément le poids exact sur PS5 ou Xbox Series X|S.
Sur une PS5 , le SSD de 825 Go laisse bien moins d’espace réellement disponible une fois le système installé. Un fichier de 180 à 200 Go pour GTA 6 pourrait occuper près d’un quart du stockage, surtout problématique sur PS5 Digital. Même constat sur Xbox Series S , dont le SSD de 512 Go est vite saturé.
Notebookcheck souligne que l’extension de stockage sur PS5 et Xbox est devenue coûteuse avec la hausse des prix des composants. Entre SSD M.2 certifiés pour PS5 et cartes d’extension propriétaires pour Xbox, il faudra peut-être choisir entre investir ou désinstaller plusieurs AAA pour faire de la place.
Autre contrainte, les joueurs soumis à une limite de données internet mensuelle. Sans disque complet en Blu-ray et avec des versions souvent réduites à un code de téléchargement, un éventuel téléchargement de 150 à 200 Go pèsera lourd sur le forfait, surtout si des mises à jour massives suivent le lancement.
La bonne nouvelle, c’est que Rockstar a prévu un préchargement dès le 12 novembre 2026. Vous aurez une semaine pour libérer de l’espace, lancer le téléchargement en heures creuses et éviter de saturer votre connexion avant de plonger dans Leonida le 19 novembre.

GTA 6 pourrait nécessiter un espace de stockage particulièrement important sur PS5 et Xbox. Une nouvelle fuite évoque une version du jeu dépassant les 200 Go, à quelques semaines de sa sortie prévue le 19 novembre. Mais cette taille ne correspond pas nécessairement à celle du jeu commercialisé.
Les joueurs devront-ils faire de la place sur leur console avant de découvrir GTA 6 ? Alors que la sortie du prochain titre de Rockstar Games approche, de nouvelles informations circulent concernant son poids sur les disques durs.
À l'origine de ces révélations, Cyberleek, qui affirme posséder une version de développement du jeu dépassant les 200 Go. Cette personne, qui diffuse déjà des extraits de gameplay, menace de rendre accessible cette version jouable si la cryptomonnaie qu'elle promeut atteint une capitalisation de 30 millions de dollars.
Aucune confirmation officielle de Rockstar Games ne permet toutefois d'établir que la version finale de GTA 6 occupera autant d'espace.
L'hypothèse d'un téléchargement particulièrement volumineux n'est pas surprenante au regard des ambitions affichées pour ce nouvel épisode.
Selon Rob Nelson, codirecteur de Rockstar North, la carte de GTA 6 serait environ deux fois plus grande que celle de GTA 5. Le niveau de détail annoncé pour Vice City et les autres territoires de Leonida pourrait également peser sur les besoins de stockage.
À titre de comparaison, la version améliorée de GTA 5 nécessite environ 95 Go sur PS5, contre 105 Go sur PC. Certains épisodes de Call of Duty: Black Ops dépassent déjà la barre des 200 Go.
Mais les versions de développement d'un jeu vidéo contiennent souvent des fichiers et des outils absents de la version commerciale. Des opérations de compression et d'optimisation peuvent également réduire considérablement leur taille.
Les joueurs ayant précommandé le titre devraient pouvoir commencer son téléchargement dès le 12 novembre, soit une semaine avant sa sortie annoncée le 19 novembre.
